answers.prompt: How consistently are important business metrics defined across teams?

selectedOption.description: Core metrics have documented definitions, identified owners, and are used consistently across most reporting.

answers.prompt: How are recurring reports and dashboards produced?

selectedOption.description: Most recurring reporting follows standardized processes and scheduled data refreshes, with documented handling for common exceptions.

answers.prompt: How does the organization detect and address data-quality problems?

selectedOption.description: Important datasets have defined validation checks, accountable owners, and documented processes for resolving issues.

answers.prompt: How directly does reporting support business decisions?

selectedOption.description: Reports and dashboards are designed around specific business questions, decision points, and accountable users.

answers.prompt: How are repetitive operational tasks currently performed?

selectedOption.description: Some tasks use templates, macros, or point solutions, but the overall process still depends on manual coordination.

answers.prompt: How are handoffs between people, teams, or systems managed?

selectedOption.description: Some handoffs use shared tools or checklists, but delays and missed steps still require frequent manual intervention.

answers.prompt: How are exceptions and unusual cases handled?

selectedOption.description: Common exceptions are recognized, but resolution steps are only partially documented or inconsistently followed.

answers.prompt: How is the success of an automated workflow evaluated?

selectedOption.description: Teams track some operational measures, but baselines and expected outcomes are not consistently defined.

answers.prompt: How are cloud services selected for new solutions?

selectedOption.description: Service selection follows defined criteria that consider business requirements, integration, security, cost, scalability, and support needs.

answers.prompt: How are development, testing, and production environments managed?

selectedOption.description: Development, testing, and production environments are clearly separated, with controlled configuration and repeatable deployment processes.

answers.prompt: How are cloud costs understood and controlled?

selectedOption.description: Cloud costs are tracked by service, project, or owner, with budgets, alerts, and periodic optimization reviews.

answers.prompt: How well can cloud solutions adapt to growth, failure, or changing requirements?

selectedOption.description: Solutions are designed with clear service boundaries, appropriate scaling, monitoring, backups, and documented recovery expectations.

answers.prompt: How are access permissions managed?

selectedOption.description: Access follows documented roles, least-privilege principles, approval processes, and periodic reviews.

answers.prompt: How are system health, failures, and service performance monitored?

selectedOption.description: Important services have defined health indicators, actionable alerts, accountable responders, and documented escalation procedures.

answers.prompt: How are production changes reviewed and deployed?

selectedOption.description: Production changes follow version control, peer review, automated validation, approval, and documented deployment procedures.

answers.prompt: How prepared is the organization to recover from failures or disruptions?

selectedOption.description: Critical systems have documented recovery objectives, tested backups, assigned owners, and defined continuity procedures.

answers.prompt: How ready is the organization’s information for AI-enabled use?

selectedOption.description: Some information is centralized, but content quality, ownership, versioning, and searchability are inconsistent.

answers.prompt: How are AI use cases selected?

selectedOption.description: Teams experiment with promising use cases, but prioritization, ownership, and expected value are inconsistent.

answers.prompt: How are AI-generated outputs reviewed and trusted?

selectedOption.description: Human review is encouraged, but standards vary by user, team, or use case.

answers.prompt: How are AI-enabled workflows monitored after implementation?

selectedOption.description: Teams review issues when they arise, but monitoring and ownership are not consistently defined.

answers.prompt: How well do internal technical capabilities match the systems the organization depends on?

selectedOption.description: Internal capabilities are aligned to the organization’s core systems, with clear escalation paths for specialized or infrequent needs.

answers.prompt: How clearly are technical responsibilities assigned?

selectedOption.description: Critical systems have documented owners, support responsibilities, decision rights, and escalation paths.

answers.prompt: How does the organization decide which technical problems to manage internally versus through external support?

selectedOption.description: The organization has defined support boundaries based on expertise, urgency, system criticality, cost, and contractual responsibilities.

answers.prompt: How resilient is the organization’s technical knowledge and staffing model?

selectedOption.description: Critical knowledge is documented, responsibilities have backups, and capacity or skills gaps are reviewed periodically.

actions.title: Select one bounded workflow
actions.description: Choose a high-volume, rules-based process with clear pain, identifiable owners, and measurable outcomes.

actions.title: Map the process and establish a baseline
actions.description: Document inputs, outputs, handoffs, delays, common exceptions, cycle time, effort, failure rate, and rework.

actions.title: Select a repeatable process with clear rules
actions.description: Prioritize a process with meaningful volume, stable inputs, and a measurable operational outcome.

actions.title: Automate the normal path
actions.description: Implement the stable portion while routing exceptions to accountable people.

deferredInvestments: End-to-end automation of an undocumented process

model.name: Internally led with targeted specialists
model.summary: Keep architecture and delivery internally owned while using specialists for narrow capability gaps.
recommendations: Use specialists for uncommon needs such as AI governance, cloud security, or advanced integration.
Avoid broad managed-service contracts unless operational capacity is the real constraint.
Retain internal decision rights and operating knowledge.
